summary: Extracted the Claude API retry proxy out of the personal claude-config repository into a standalone, public, pip-installable package named claude-retry-proxy. The proxy is a stdlib-only HTTP server (ThreadingHTTPServer on localhost) that forwards requests to the upstream ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL read from ~/.claude/settings.json, retries 503 responses with exponential backoff, and logs every request to a JSONL trace file; a CLI manager (start/stop/status) swaps the base URL in settings.json to localhost while the proxy runs and restores it on stop, with lock-file crash recovery and cross-platform PID liveness and kill via ctypes on Windows. Key decisions: hardcoded ~/.claude/settings.json as the sole URL store with no env-var fallback, package and console command both named claude-retry-proxy (renamed from claude-proxy), Python 3.8 plus setuptools 64 floor for PEP 660 src-layout editable installs, zero runtime dependencies, MIT license. The server's upstream-URL resolution was moved from import time into main() so direct invocation reads settings at runtime and emits a clean error; trace and state files get a POSIX-only 0o600 chmod (a near-no-op on Windows, documented). The 24-test suite was ported from claude-config with the non-portable deploy-protection test dropped, the test runner's prerequisite block rewritten to use importlib find_spec, SourceFileLoader replaced with direct imports, and dead auth-token plumbing removed with probe_ok readiness guards. Implementation is complete and tested at 23 of 24 passing; the sole failure is a pre-existing upstream Windows port-bind readiness race (the CLI TCP probe can report success on an occupied port) left as a documented future-work TODO alongside the response-streaming has no size cap issue.
